public_payload.normalized_proposition: Cancer will not be eradicated within a decade, and curing mental illness within a decade is fantasy.

statement.excerpt: Cancer is more than one thing, and it will take more than a decade to eradicate it; the bit about curing mental illness (and some other things) that quickly is absolute fantasy.
statement.document_title: Breaking: Eli Lilly CEO becomes latest to push back on Dario Amodei’s ludicrous, Elizabeth Holmes-like medical claims

from_speaker: Cancer is more than one thing
it will take more than a decade to eradicate it
our_interpretation: Assess the two future commitments separately: cancer will not be eradicated within ten years, and mental illness will not be broadly cured within ten years.
Use 2036-11-12, ten years after publication, as the deadline.
Read eradication as eliminating cancer as an ongoing disease burden, rather than producing a cure for an individual patient or subtype.
Read curing mental illness as broad, durable cures across the category, rather than symptom improvement or individual remission.
'Cancer is more than one thing' is a factual premise. Establishing that premise does not settle either forecast.
'Some other things' is unspecified and is not expanded into additional independently scored predictions.
criteria.support_condition: At the deadline, authoritative evidence establishes both that cancer has not been eradicated and that mental illness has not been broadly cured.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Cancer is eradicated and mental illness is broadly cured within the decade. Achievement of only one would contradict that component; a mixed outcome would require evidence settling the other component as well.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Clinical and population evidence establishing cancer eradication and broad mental-illness cures within the decade could contradict the forecast early. Otherwise, assess each component at November 2036.
